androidDeckTracker.onboarding.intro: Please read the instructions below to set up Firestone on your phone. It's a one-time setup, and we'll guide you through it to make it as easy as possible.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.overlayPer: The deck list is display-only, so it does not take taps meant for Hearthstone. A small button shows or hides it.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.pairNotRea: The code screen closed before the code was sent. Show the code again, leave that screen open, and type the 6 digits in the Firestone notification.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.pairWaitin: Leave the code on screen, then type the 6 digits here.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.pairWrongC: That code did not work. Type the code shown on screen.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.readyBody: Start a Hearthstone game. The deck list appears over the match.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.setupBody: Tap Continue when you are ready for the next screen.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.shizukuIns: Shizuku lets Firestone read Hearthstone's log files.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.shizukuSta: Open wireless debugging, start Shizuku, then come back. You need to do this again after every reboot.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.shizukuSto: Shizuku stopped, usually after a reboot. Tap Set up to open it. On a trusted Wi-Fi it can start itself next time.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.signedIn: Signed in as {name}. Finished games are saved to this account.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.signedInNo: Your games are now synchronized to your account, and can be retrieved from the desktop application.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.signInBody: Tap to sign in with Battle.net, which will let you save all your games to your Firestone account. Your Battle.net info is never shared with Firestone.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepAllowI: Tap Continue. Android opens a setting for Firestone. Turn on Allow from this source, then come back here.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepDevelo: Tap Continue. On the phone info screen, scroll to Build number and tap it 7 times, until the phone says developer options are on. Then come back.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepGrant: Tap Continue. Android will ask whether Firestone can use the helper. Tap Allow.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepInstal: Tap Continue. Android will ask you to install the helper Firestone needs. Confirm the install, then come back to this screen.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepNearby: Tap Continue. Android will ask to let Firestone find wireless debugging on this phone. Tap Allow.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepOverla: Tap Continue to let Firestone show on top of the game. Find Firestone in the list that will appear, and allow it to display over other apps. Then come back here.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepPair: Tap Show the code. Tap on "Wireless debugging", then tap "Pair device with pairing code". Leave that screen open. Tap the Firestone notification and type the 6-digit code there.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepStart: Tap Continue to start the helper. Stay on this screen. It takes a few seconds. If a pairing code is needed, the next step explains it.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepUnsupp: This Android version cannot run the tracker.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.stepWirele: Tap Continue. Find Wireless debugging and turn the switch on. If the phone asks about this Wi-Fi, allow it. Then come back.
androidDeckTracker.onboarding.title: Set up the deck tracker

settings.general.launch.disable-hardware: Draw the app's windows and overlays on the CPU instead of the graphics card. This lowers the app's memory use, but animations and scrolling can use more CPU. Can also help if you see display glitches or blank windows. Requires restarting the app.
settings.general.launch.disable-low-memo: By default, the app renders its windows and overlay with smaller graphics buffers, which saves about 100 MB of memory in games. Turn this on if windows or the overlay look wrong or scroll poorly. Takes effect the next time the app starts.
settings.general.launch.disable-overlay-: By default, the in-game overlay is sent to the game directly through the graphics card, which uses much less CPU. Turn this on if the overlay doesn't show up, looks wrong, or blocks clicks in the game. Takes effect the next time Hearthstone starts.
settings.general.localization.ai-text: When enabled, missing translations are filled with AI-generated text. Community translations always take priority. AI strings may be imperfect, and English is still used if no AI translation exists.

website.docs.pages.mods.sections.configu:
Players can change your mod's options from Firestone. Bind each option with Config.Bind in a section named Firestone. After the plugin has started once, Firestone adds a page under Settings > Mods, using the mod's name.

Only sections named Firestone, or Firestone followed by a group such as Firestone.Replay, are shown. The General metadata (Name, Guid, Version, DownloadLink, Description) stays on the mods list.

Config.Bind("Firestone", "EnableFoo", true, "Enable Foo\nTurns the feature on.");

Config.Bind("Firestone.Replay", "Speed", 1f,
    new ConfigDescription("Playback speed", new AcceptableValueRange<float>(0.5f, 4f)));

Config.Bind("Firestone", "Mode", Mode.Fast, "Which mode to use");

The first line of the description is the label. Further lines are the tooltip. Firestone.Replay is a group titled Replay. A plain Firestone section has no group heading. Settings appear in the order of the Bind calls.

The page shows up once the plugin has run, because that is when BepInEx writes the cfg. Changing a value in Firestone updates that file, and the plugin reads it the next time Hearthstone starts. If the game is already running, Firestone asks the player to restart it.

website.faq.sections.smart-app-control.b:
Windows 11 Smart App Control can block Firestone's memory-reader file (OverwolfUnitySpy.dll). When that happens:

  • You're not seeing widgets in-game
  • Restarting Firestone or Hearthstone does not help
  • The Firestone main window (collection, stats) can still work

To check whether Smart App Control is on: open Windows Security → App & browser control → Smart App Control settings. See Microsoft's Smart App Control FAQ.

Update to the latest Firestone. Recent releases sign the memory-reader plugin so Windows can allow it. If you are already on the latest version and overlays are still empty, please report a bug from the app.
